quiz_elements.question: A retailer needs additional compute capacity during a weekend promotion and less capacity afterward. Which cloud benefit meets this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: Elasticity: Resources can expand and contract as demand changes. High availability: Keeps a workload accessible despite failures; it does not describe changing capacity. Economies of scale: Aggregated provider demand reduces unit costs; it does not describe demand tracking. Global reach: Supports deployment near worldwide users; it does not describe temporary capacity changes.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to test a new product idea this afternoon without waiting for hardware procurement. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud supports this goal?
quiz_elements.explanation: Data residency: Concerns where data is stored rather than the speed of experimentation. Fault tolerance: Concerns continued operation through failures. Reserved capacity: Concerns capacity or pricing commitments rather than immediate experimentation. Agility: Provisioning resources quickly enables rapid experiments.

quiz_elements.question: A company buys servers for expected peak demand, but most servers are idle for much of the year. Which cloud advantage addresses this problem?
answers: Use a fixed server count for every workload
Select a discounted commitment for the existing fixed capacity
quiz_elements.explanation: Use a fixed server count for every workload: Does not respond to changing demand. Select a discounted commitment for the existing fixed capacity: A discount can lower a unit price but does not adapt capacity to workload demand. Provision capacity as demand changes: Scaling resources reduces the need to predict peak capacity far in advance. Purchase hardware before deployment: Retains the capacity forecasting problem.

quiz_elements.question: A startup wants to pay for compute resources as it uses them instead of buying a server fleet before launch. Which financial change does this represent?
answers: Replacing operational expense with capital expense
Paying a fixed price for unlimited usage
Replacing fixed expense with variable expense
quiz_elements.explanation: Paying a fixed price for unlimited usage: AWS consumption pricing does not provide unlimited usage for a fixed price. Replacing fixed expense with variable expense: Consumption-based spending replaces a substantial infrastructure purchase. Replacing operational expense with capital expense: This reverses the change described. Increasing hardware depreciation: Owned hardware depreciation is not the cloud benefit described.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Replacing fixed expense with variable expense

quiz_elements.question: Why can a large cloud provider offer economies of scale to its customers?
answers: Each customer builds a separate physical data center
Each workload uses the same instance size
Customers prepay for all future consumption
It aggregates demand from many customers
quiz_elements.explanation: It aggregates demand from many customers: Large aggregate demand creates efficiencies that can lower unit prices. Each customer builds a separate physical data center: Separate facilities do not explain shared provider scale. Each workload uses the same instance size: Workloads can use different sizes; uniform sizing is not the cause. Customers prepay for all future consumption: Prepayment is not required to benefit from provider scale.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: It aggregates demand from many customers

quiz_elements.question: A company expands into a new continent and wants to deploy its application near local users quickly. Which AWS Cloud benefit is most relevant?
quiz_elements.explanation: Economies of scale: Provider scale can reduce unit costs but does not describe rapid geographic expansion. Elasticity: Elasticity adapts capacity to demand rather than directly providing worldwide deployment locations. Vertical scaling: Changes resource size rather than geographic placement. Global reach: AWS infrastructure in multiple geographic locations supports fast expansion.

quiz_elements.question: Which cost should a company include when comparing its on-premises environment with AWS?
answers: Only the purchase price of application software
Only the number of employee user accounts
Only the advertised hourly price of an EC2 instance
Power and cooling for its data center
quiz_elements.explanation: Only the number of employee user accounts: Account count alone does not capture infrastructure cost. Only the advertised hourly price of an EC2 instance: A single cloud rate does not capture the complete comparison. Power and cooling for its data center: Infrastructure overhead contributes to the total cost of ownership. Only the purchase price of application software: Software alone omits hardware and operational expenses.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Power and cooling for its data center

quiz_elements.question: An operations team spends much of its time replacing disks and installing physical servers. Which cloud benefit allows the team to spend more time on customer features?
answers: Savings from a term compute commitment
Capacity assurance from an Availability Zone reservation
quiz_elements.explanation: Capacity assurance from an Availability Zone reservation: A capacity reservation provides resource availability rather than defining who maintains hardware. Reduced work operating physical infrastructure: AWS operates the physical cloud infrastructure, freeing time for business work. Savings from a term compute commitment: A price commitment changes compute economics rather than physical maintenance responsibilities. Cost allocation through resource tags: Tagging provides spending attribution rather than removing maintenance work.

quiz_elements.question: An EC2 instance has consistently low CPU and memory usage. The application meets its performance requirements on a smaller instance. What should the company do to reduce cost?
answers: Keep the size and add a capacity reservation
quiz_elements.explanation: Rightsize the instance: Selecting capacity that meets measured requirements reduces unused resources. Move to a larger instance: Adds capacity that the workload does not require. Add an identical instance: Adds cost without a demonstrated demand increase. Keep the size and add a capacity reservation: A capacity reservation does not remove oversized capacity.

quiz_elements.question: A company uses eligible software licenses it already owns for a workload on AWS. Which licensing approach is this?
quiz_elements.explanation: License included: Obtains the license as part of the AWS service offering. Spot pricing: Describes a compute purchasing option, not license ownership. Consolidated billing: Combines billing across accounts, not software license ownership. Bring Your Own License (BYOL): Reuses existing eligible licenses under their licensing terms.

quiz_elements.question: A company selects an AWS offering whose charge includes the required commercial software license. Which licensing approach is it using?
quiz_elements.explanation: Rehosting: Describes a migration strategy rather than a licensing approach. Volume pricing: Describes usage-based discounts rather than included licenses. License included: The offering provides licensing as part of its price. Bring Your Own License (BYOL): Requires eligible licenses that the customer brings.

quiz_elements.question: A company automates the shutdown of development compute resources outside working hours. What is a direct economic benefit?
answers: Lower storage charges from leaving attached volumes allocated
Lower prices for every running instance through a capacity reservation
Lower daytime compute demand caused by assigning cost allocation tags
Reduced spending on unused running resources
quiz_elements.explanation: Lower daytime compute demand caused by assigning cost allocation tags: Tags label costs and do not change application demand. Reduced spending on unused running resources: Scheduling resource use avoids paying for idle compute periods. Lower storage charges from leaving attached volumes allocated: Stopping compute does not by itself remove charges for retained storage. Lower prices for every running instance through a capacity reservation: Capacity reservations provide capacity assurance rather than a blanket price discount.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Reduced spending on unused running resources

quiz_elements.question: A team reviews incident reports and improves its deployment procedures after each release. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar is most directly addressed?
quiz_elements.explanation: Operational excellence: Focuses on improving operational processes and learning from operational events. Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Sustainability: Focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads. Performance efficiency: Focuses on choosing and using resources to meet performance requirements.

quiz_elements.question: A company encrypts customer records and limits access to authorized staff. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar does this address?
quiz_elements.explanation: Cost optimization: Focuses on delivering business value at an appropriate cost. Performance efficiency: Focuses on choosing and using resources to meet performance requirements. Operational excellence: Focuses on improving operational processes and learning from operational events. Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets.

quiz_elements.question: A company regularly tests whether its application can recover after a component failure. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar is most relevant?
quiz_elements.explanation: Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Sustainability: Focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads. Reliability: Focuses on consistent workload operation and recovery from failures. Cost optimization: Focuses on delivering business value at an appropriate cost.

quiz_elements.question: A team compares compute options and selects the option that meets application latency requirements efficiently. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar is most relevant?
quiz_elements.explanation: Reliability: Focuses on consistent workload operation and recovery from failures. Performance efficiency: Focuses on choosing and using resources to meet performance requirements. Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Operational excellence: Focuses on improving operational processes and learning from operational events.

quiz_elements.question: A company removes unused resources and measures the cost of delivering each business transaction. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar guides this work?
quiz_elements.explanation: Cost optimization: Focuses on delivering business value at an appropriate cost. Reliability: Focuses on consistent workload operation and recovery from failures. Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Operational excellence: Focuses on improving operational processes and learning from operational events.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to reduce the energy and resource consumption associated with its cloud workload. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar addresses this objective?
quiz_elements.explanation: Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Reliability: Focuses on consistent workload operation and recovery from failures. Operational excellence: Focuses on improving operational processes and learning from operational events. Sustainability: Focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants a structured review of its workload against AWS architectural best practices. Which AWS resource should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Organizations: Manages accounts and governance rather than conducting workload reviews. AWS Database Migration Service: Moves or replicates database data rather than reviewing workloads. AWS Well-Architected Tool: Reviews workloads using questions organized by the framework pillars. AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates prospective service costs rather than reviewing all pillars.

quiz_elements.question: A team monitors operational outcomes and uses the findings to improve how it runs a workload. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar covers this activity?
quiz_elements.explanation: Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Operational excellence: Focuses on improving operational processes and learning from operational events. Cost optimization: Focuses on delivering business value at an appropriate cost. Sustainability: Focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads.

quiz_elements.question: A business wants its application to continue delivering its intended function when a component becomes unavailable. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar is most relevant?
quiz_elements.explanation: Reliability: Focuses on consistent workload operation and recovery from failures. Performance efficiency: Focuses on choosing and using resources to meet performance requirements. Cost optimization: Focuses on delivering business value at an appropriate cost. Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets.

quiz_elements.question: A company reviews its resource choices as demand and available technology change to maintain application performance. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar supports this review?
quiz_elements.explanation: Operational excellence: Focuses on improving operational processes and learning from operational events. Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Sustainability: Focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads. Performance efficiency: Focuses on choosing and using resources to meet performance requirements.

quiz_elements.question: An organization wants to minimize the environmental impact per transaction processed by its application. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar addresses this goal most directly?
quiz_elements.explanation: Reliability: Focuses on consistent workload operation and recovery from failures. Security: Focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Sustainability: Focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads. Cost optimization: Focuses on delivering business value at an appropriate cost.

quiz_elements.question: A workload review evaluates security, reliability, performance, operations, cost, and environmental impact. Which framework provides these review areas?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS consolidated billing: Combines and allocates account charges rather than reviewing workload quality. AWS Well-Architected Framework: Its six pillars provide these workload quality dimensions. AWS Cloud Adoption Framework: Guides organizational cloud transformation using perspectives. AWS shared responsibility model: Divides security responsibilities between AWS and customers.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs to identify gaps in organizational cloud readiness and prioritize its transformation roadmap. Which AWS framework should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF): Helps assess readiness and plan organizational transformation. AWS Well-Architected Framework: Reviews workload quality rather than the entire transformation roadmap. AWS shared responsibility model: Defines security responsibilities rather than adoption readiness. AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates selected AWS service costs rather than organizational readiness.

quiz_elements.question: A company creates a cloud training program and changes team responsibilities to support cloud adoption. Which AWS CAF perspective is most relevant?
quiz_elements.explanation: Platform: Focuses on building and modernizing the technical platform. Security: Focuses on protecting data and workloads. Operations: Focuses on delivering and operating cloud services. People: Covers workforce, organizational structure, culture, and leadership.

quiz_elements.question: Executives want cloud investments to support new revenue opportunities and business outcomes. Which AWS CAF perspective addresses this goal?
quiz_elements.explanation: Operations: Addresses ongoing delivery of cloud services. Security: Addresses confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Business: Connects cloud investments with business transformation outcomes. Platform: Addresses the technical cloud platform.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to coordinate cloud initiatives, measure their benefits, and manage transformation risks. Which AWS CAF perspective should it consult?
quiz_elements.explanation: Operations: Focuses on service delivery and ongoing operations. Governance: Coordinates initiatives while managing benefits and transformation risk. People: Focuses on workforce and culture. Platform: Focuses on scalable cloud foundations and workload modernization.

quiz_elements.question: An organization is building a scalable cloud foundation and modernizing existing workloads. Which AWS CAF perspective most directly supports this work?
quiz_elements.explanation: Platform: Addresses cloud foundations and technical workload modernization. Business: Focuses on investment outcomes rather than platform capabilities. People: Focuses on workforce readiness rather than platform engineering. Governance: Focuses on coordination and transformation risk rather than platform construction.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its cloud data. Which AWS CAF perspective covers these goals?
quiz_elements.explanation: Business: Addresses business outcomes from cloud investments. People: Addresses workforce, culture, and leadership. Governance: Addresses coordination and transformation risk rather than these protection goals. Security: Addresses protection of data and cloud workloads.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants its cloud services to meet agreed business service levels during daily operation. Which AWS CAF perspective is most relevant?
quiz_elements.explanation: People: Addresses workforce and culture. Platform: Addresses cloud foundation and workload modernization. Operations: Addresses reliable delivery of cloud services to meet business needs. Business: Addresses cloud investment outcomes.

quiz_elements.question: A company moves an existing application to EC2 without changing its application code or architecture. Which migration strategy is this?
quiz_elements.explanation: Retire: Decommissions the application. Rehost: Moves a workload with minimal or no application changes. Refactor: Redesigns the application to use cloud-native capabilities. Repurchase: Replaces the application with another product.

quiz_elements.question: A company moves an application database to a managed database service while preserving the core application architecture. Which migration strategy best describes this approach?
quiz_elements.explanation: Replatform: Introduces targeted cloud optimizations while preserving the core architecture. Retain: Keeps the application in its existing environment. Repurchase: Replaces the application with a different product. Retire: Removes the application from use.

quiz_elements.question: A company replaces its internally hosted CRM application with a SaaS product. Which migration strategy is this?
quiz_elements.explanation: Rehost: Moves the existing application with minimal changes. Refactor: Redesigns the existing application rather than purchasing a replacement. Retain: Leaves the existing application in its source environment. Repurchase: Replaces an existing application with a new product, such as SaaS.

quiz_elements.question: A company redesigns a monolithic application to use cloud-native components as part of its migration. Which migration strategy is it using?
quiz_elements.explanation: Retain: Keeps the application in its source environment. Repurchase: Replaces the application with a different product. Refactor: Changes the application architecture to take advantage of cloud-native capabilities. Rehost: Moves the existing application largely unchanged.

quiz_elements.question: A company discovers that an old reporting application has no users and no remaining business value. Which migration strategy is appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: Retain: Keeps the application in its current environment. Retire: Decommissions an application that no longer provides value. Rehost: Moves the application but continues paying to operate it. Replatform: Optimizes the application but continues operating it.

quiz_elements.question: A manufacturing application depends on specialized local hardware. The company decides to keep it on premises for now. Which migration strategy is this?
quiz_elements.explanation: Retain: Keeps an application in its source environment when migration is unsuitable or premature. Retire: Removes the application from use. Repurchase: Replaces it with another product. Rehost: Moves it into AWS with minimal application changes.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs to replicate changes from its source database to AWS while the source continues serving users during migration. Which service is designed for this task?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS): Moves database data and can continuously replicate changes while the source database remains operational. AWS DataSync: Transfers file and object data; it is not the database change replication service described. AWS Migration Hub: Tracks migration progress rather than itself replicating database changes. AWS Storage Gateway: Provides hybrid storage access rather than database transaction replication.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs a data-driven business case for moving its on-premises infrastructure to AWS. Which AWS service is most appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: Migration Evaluator: Uses existing environment data to support a migration business case. AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates selected AWS configurations, but does not itself assess the existing on-premises estate. AWS Cost Explorer: Analyzes incurred AWS costs rather than assessing an on-premises estate. AWS Trusted Advisor: Provides AWS environment best-practice checks rather than an on-premises migration business case.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants hands-on expert assistance to plan and carry out a cloud transformation program. Which AWS offering should it consider?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch: Provides observability rather than a consulting team. AWS Professional Services: Provides consulting expertise for cloud transformation and migration. AWS Pricing Calculator: Produces estimates rather than delivering a consulting engagement. AWS Cost and Usage Reports: Provide billing data rather than migration expertise.

quiz_elements.question: A company runs an application partly in its data center and partly on AWS. Which deployment model is it using?
quiz_elements.explanation: Hybrid cloud: Combines cloud resources with existing infrastructure. All-in cloud: Places the application resources in the cloud rather than retaining on-premises components. On-premises deployment: Does not describe the AWS-hosted portion. Software as a service only: Describes an application delivery model rather than this infrastructure placement.

quiz_elements.question: A developer uses virtual machines and controls their operating systems and application software. Which cloud service model does this most closely represent?
quiz_elements.explanation: Software as a service (SaaS): Delivers an application without this infrastructure management responsibility. Platform as a service (PaaS): Abstracts more of the underlying infrastructure and operating system management. On-premises hosting: Describes customer premises rather than a cloud service model. Infrastructure as a service (IaaS): Provides infrastructure while the customer manages operating systems and applications.

quiz_elements.question: A business subscribes to an online application and does not manage the servers or operating systems that run it. Which cloud service model is this?
quiz_elements.explanation: Bring Your Own License (BYOL): Describes licensing rather than the service delivery model. Hybrid cloud: Describes deployment placement rather than application management responsibility. Software as a service (SaaS): Delivers a ready-to-use application with infrastructure managed by its provider. Infrastructure as a service (IaaS): Typically requires the customer to manage operating systems and deployed applications.

quiz_elements.question: Which statement best defines scalability, as distinct from elasticity, availability, and fault tolerance?
answers: The ability to keep a service accessible with minimal downtime
The ability to keep operating when an individual component fails
The ability to add capacity as workload demand grows
The ability to automatically add and remove capacity as demand fluctuates
quiz_elements.explanation: The ability to add capacity as workload demand grows: Scalability describes increasing resource capacity to support growth. The ability to automatically add and remove capacity as demand fluctuates: Describes elasticity, which includes adapting capacity in both directions. The ability to keep a service accessible with minimal downtime: Describes availability rather than capacity growth. The ability to keep operating when an individual component fails: Describes fault tolerance rather than capacity growth.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: The ability to add capacity as workload demand grows

quiz_elements.question: A company deploys application components across multiple independent failure locations. Which outcome is this intended to improve?
quiz_elements.explanation: High availability: Independent failure locations reduce the risk of application downtime from a location failure. Elasticity: Concerns increasing and decreasing capacity with demand. Agility: Concerns how quickly an organization can experiment and deliver changes. Economies of scale: Concern the cost efficiencies of aggregate provider demand.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to lower the cost of trials by creating temporary environments and deleting them when each trial ends. Which cloud benefit supports this practice?
answers: Maintaining peak capacity throughout the year
quiz_elements.explanation: Maintaining peak capacity throughout the year: Retains unused capacity and its cost. Purchasing servers before each trial: Increases procurement effort and upfront expense. Keeping every trial environment running: Continues paying for environments that are no longer needed. Rapid provisioning with consumption-based spending: Temporary resources support experimentation without permanent hardware investment.

quiz_elements.question: A company plans to use its existing commercial software licenses on AWS. What should it verify first?
answers: That all AWS instance types automatically include the license
That consolidated billing transfers software license ownership
That Spot Instances remove vendor licensing requirements
That its license terms permit the planned AWS deployment
quiz_elements.explanation: That consolidated billing transfers software license ownership: Consolidated billing does not transfer license ownership. That Spot Instances remove vendor licensing requirements: Compute discounts do not remove licensing obligations. That its license terms permit the planned AWS deployment: BYOL eligibility depends on vendor terms and deployment requirements. That all AWS instance types automatically include the license: License inclusion depends on the offering, not every instance type.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: That its license terms permit the planned AWS deployment

quiz_elements.question: A finance team compares an AWS proposal with the company data center budget. Which approach provides a more complete total cost comparison?
answers: Compare only the number of physical servers
Compare only the proposed hourly compute rates
Compare infrastructure, licensing, facilities, and ongoing operations costs
quiz_elements.explanation: Compare only network latency: Latency is a performance measure rather than a total cost measure. Compare infrastructure, licensing, facilities, and ongoing operations costs: A total cost comparison includes more than compute purchase prices. Compare only the number of physical servers: Server counts ignore different capacities and operational costs. Compare only the proposed hourly compute rates: Compute rates alone omit storage, network, licensing, and operating expenses.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Compare infrastructure, licensing, facilities, and ongoing operations costs

quiz_elements.question: Which actions use cloud elasticity to control resource consumption? (Select TWO.)
answers: Purchase a fixed server fleet for the next five years
Move billing responsibility to another department
Add compute resources when demand increases
Remove unneeded compute resources when demand decreases
Maintain peak capacity during all low-demand periods
quiz_elements.explanation: Purchase a fixed server fleet for the next five years: Locks in capacity rather than providing demand-based elasticity. Move billing responsibility to another department: Changes accounting ownership rather than resource capacity. Add compute resources when demand increases: Scaling out addresses higher demand. Remove unneeded compute resources when demand decreases: Scaling in reduces idle capacity. Maintain peak capacity during all low-demand periods: Retains idle resources rather than adapting capacity.
correct_answers: Add compute resources when demand increases
Remove unneeded compute resources when demand decreases

quiz_elements.question: Which costs are associated with operating an on-premises data center? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon S3 request charges: These are AWS service charges rather than local data center costs. Physical server maintenance: Owned physical servers require upkeep. Electricity and cooling: Running a data center incurs facilities costs. AWS Savings Plans commitments: These are AWS purchasing commitments rather than local facilities expenses. AWS Support plan charges: These are AWS support expenses rather than data center operations costs.
correct_answers: Physical server maintenance
Electricity and cooling

quiz_elements.question: Which actions support the AWS Well-Architected Reliability pillar? (Select TWO.)
answers: Distribute resources across independent failure locations
Select a software licensing payment model
quiz_elements.explanation: Test recovery procedures: Testing validates that recovery works when needed. Distribute resources across independent failure locations: Redundancy reduces exposure to one location failure. Select a software licensing payment model: Licensing is an economic decision rather than a recovery mechanism. Allocate monthly spending to departments: Cost attribution does not provide recovery capability. Train employees in procurement processes: Procurement training does not establish workload resilience.
correct_answers: Test recovery procedures
Distribute resources across independent failure locations

quiz_elements.question: Which goals belong to the AWS Well-Architected Security pillar? (Select TWO.)
answers: Select resources solely by lowest hourly price
Minimize the environmental impact per transaction
quiz_elements.explanation: Control access to workload resources: Identity and access control protect resources. Reduce invoice processing time: This is an administrative objective. Select resources solely by lowest hourly price: Price alone does not establish security. Minimize the environmental impact per transaction: This is primarily a sustainability objective. Protect sensitive information: Data protection is a security objective.
correct_answers: Protect sensitive information
Control access to workload resources

quiz_elements.question: Which actions are consistent with cloud cost optimization? (Select TWO.)
answers: Use a larger instance to reserve headroom without examining utilization
Choose On-Demand pricing for stable usage without assessing commitment discounts
Base the storage class choice only on its price per stored gigabyte
Remove resources that no longer deliver business value
Match resource sizes to measured workload requirements
quiz_elements.explanation: Remove resources that no longer deliver business value: Avoids paying for unneeded resources. Match resource sizes to measured workload requirements: Rightsizing avoids capacity expense beyond measured requirements. Use a larger instance to reserve headroom without examining utilization: Unmeasured extra headroom can add unnecessary capacity cost. Choose On-Demand pricing for stable usage without assessing commitment discounts: Stable eligible usage may benefit from commitment pricing; skipping the assessment misses that opportunity. Base the storage class choice only on its price per stored gigabyte: Ignoring retrieval and minimum-duration charges can increase total cost.
correct_answers: Remove resources that no longer deliver business value
Match resource sizes to measured workload requirements

quiz_elements.question: Which activities are associated with the AWS CAF People perspective? (Select TWO.)
answers: Operate a daily incident response queue
Develop cloud skills in the workforce
Manage organizational change during cloud adoption
quiz_elements.explanation: Configure workload encryption: This is a security implementation activity. Operate a daily incident response queue: This is an ongoing operations activity. Develop cloud skills in the workforce: Workforce readiness is part of People. Manage organizational change during cloud adoption: Culture and organizational change are part of People. Select database storage engines: This is a technical platform decision.
correct_answers: Develop cloud skills in the workforce
Manage organizational change during cloud adoption

quiz_elements.question: Which outcomes can AWS CAF help an organization pursue during cloud transformation? (Select TWO.)
answers: Generate the monthly cost and usage billing report
Define the minimum permissions in an IAM policy
Reserve EC2 capacity for an Availability Zone
quiz_elements.explanation: Improve operational efficiency: Cloud transformation can improve business operating effectiveness. Create new revenue opportunities: Cloud capabilities can support new products and business models. Reserve EC2 capacity for an Availability Zone: This is an EC2 purchasing capability rather than a CAF transformation outcome. Generate the monthly cost and usage billing report: Billing reports are service outputs rather than CAF business outcomes. Define the minimum permissions in an IAM policy: This is a security implementation detail rather than a CAF business outcome.
correct_answers: Improve operational efficiency
Create new revenue opportunities

quiz_elements.question: Which statements describe rehosting and refactoring migration strategies? (Select TWO.)
answers: Refactoring changes the application architecture to use cloud capabilities
Rehosting requires replacement with a SaaS product
Refactoring means permanently shutting down the application
Both strategies require leaving the application on premises
Rehosting moves an existing application with minimal changes
quiz_elements.explanation: Rehosting moves an existing application with minimal changes: Rehosting preserves the application while changing its hosting location. Refactoring changes the application architecture to use cloud capabilities: Refactoring involves architectural modernization. Rehosting requires replacement with a SaaS product: SaaS replacement is repurchasing. Refactoring means permanently shutting down the application: Shutdown of an unneeded application is retirement. Both strategies require leaving the application on premises: Neither is defined by retaining the source environment.
correct_answers: Rehosting moves an existing application with minimal changes
Refactoring changes the application architecture to use cloud capabilities

quiz_elements.question: Which activities help build a cloud migration business case? (Select TWO.)
answers: Include facilities and operational costs in the comparison
Use server purchase prices as the entire cost baseline
Use peak provisioned server capacity as the only measure of demand
Exclude software licensing from the assessment
quiz_elements.explanation: Include facilities and operational costs in the comparison: A complete comparison accounts for infrastructure overhead. Use server purchase prices as the entire cost baseline: This omits ongoing operating expenses. Use peak provisioned server capacity as the only measure of demand: A provisioned peak baseline alone can overstate what the workload actually needs. Exclude software licensing from the assessment: License costs can materially affect the business case. Measure utilization of existing infrastructure: Usage helps estimate suitable target capacity and cost.
correct_answers: Measure utilization of existing infrastructure
Include facilities and operational costs in the comparison

quiz_elements.question: Which statements correctly describe software licensing approaches on AWS? (Select TWO.)
answers: An EC2 instance reservation determines whether a software license is portable
BYOL is the name for obtaining a new license through an AWS service charge
Resource cost allocation tags establish compliance with vendor licensing terms
BYOL uses eligible licenses the customer already owns
License-included offerings include licensing in the service price
quiz_elements.explanation: BYOL uses eligible licenses the customer already owns: Existing licenses can be used when the vendor terms permit. License-included offerings include licensing in the service price: The offering provides licensing as part of its charge. An EC2 instance reservation determines whether a software license is portable: EC2 pricing commitments do not determine vendor license mobility. BYOL is the name for obtaining a new license through an AWS service charge: That description corresponds to a license-included offering. Resource cost allocation tags establish compliance with vendor licensing terms: Tags attribute costs rather than proving adherence to vendor license terms.
correct_answers: BYOL uses eligible licenses the customer already owns
License-included offerings include licensing in the service price

quiz_elements.question: Which practices can reduce the environmental impact of a cloud workload? (Select TWO.)
answers: Select the largest resource sizes regardless of utilization
Use dedicated physical capacity regardless of workload utilization
Delete data that no longer needs to be retained
Maintain redundant idle test environments indefinitely
quiz_elements.explanation: Select the largest resource sizes regardless of utilization: Oversizing adds unnecessary consumption. Use dedicated physical capacity regardless of workload utilization: Dedicated placement does not inherently minimize the resources consumed by useful work. Improve utilization of provisioned resources: Better utilization can reduce the resources needed for useful work. Delete data that no longer needs to be retained: Reducing unnecessary storage reduces resource consumption. Maintain redundant idle test environments indefinitely: Unused environments consume resources.
correct_answers: Improve utilization of provisioned resources
Delete data that no longer needs to be retained

quiz_elements.question: Which AWS Well-Architected pillars address the following goals: reducing environmental impact and improving operational processes? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Performance efficiency: Addresses using resources to meet performance requirements. Sustainability: Addresses environmental impact and resource efficiency. Operational excellence: Addresses how workloads are operated and improved. Security: Addresses protection of systems and information. Reliability: Addresses consistent function and recovery.
correct_answers: Sustainability
Operational excellence

quiz_elements.question: A company needs EC2 instances for a short project with unpredictable usage. It does not want an upfront payment or long-term commitment. Which purchasing option should it choose?
quiz_elements.explanation: On-Demand Instances: Provide consumption-based compute without a long-term pricing commitment. Reserved Instances: Require a term commitment in exchange for a billing discount. Savings Plans: Require a usage spending commitment over a term. Dedicated Hosts: Provide dedicated physical servers, which are not required by this scenario.

quiz_elements.question: A company processes a batch job that can restart after interruption. It wants to use spare EC2 capacity at a discounted price. Which option is most appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: On-Demand Instances: Provide flexible compute but not the spare-capacity discount described. Dedicated Hosts: Provide dedicated physical servers rather than discounted spare capacity. On-Demand Capacity Reservations: Reserve capacity in an Availability Zone rather than offering spare-capacity pricing. Spot Instances: Offer discounted spare capacity that can be interrupted.

quiz_elements.question: A company has predictable EC2 usage and can commit to a specific instance configuration for a term in exchange for a discount. Which purchasing option best fits this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: On-Demand Instances: Do not provide this term-based commitment discount. On-Demand Capacity Reservations: Reserve capacity but do not inherently provide a commitment discount. Reserved Instances: Provide a billing discount for matching EC2 usage over a committed term. Spot Instances: Use interruptible spare capacity rather than a stable term-based billing commitment.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants discounted compute pricing in exchange for committing to a consistent amount of eligible compute spending per hour. Which option should it choose?
quiz_elements.explanation: On-Demand Instances: Use standard consumption pricing without this commitment discount. Savings Plans: Exchange a qualifying hourly spending commitment for discounted usage rates. Spot Instances: Use interruptible spare capacity without a term spending commitment. On-Demand Capacity Reservations: Reserve capacity rather than providing a spending commitment discount.

quiz_elements.question: A company has software licenses tied to a physical server and needs visibility into the server used for its EC2 instances. Which option is most appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: Dedicated Hosts: Provide a dedicated physical EC2 server and host visibility for eligible server-bound licenses. Spot Instances: Provide spare instance capacity without dedicated host visibility. Regional Reserved Instances: Provide billing benefits rather than allocating a visible physical server. On-Demand Capacity Reservations: Reserve matching capacity but do not provide physical server visibility.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs assurance that a specific EC2 instance configuration will have capacity available in one Availability Zone for a planned event. Which option directly addresses this need?
quiz_elements.explanation: Compute Savings Plan: Provides a billing discount and does not reserve capacity. Regional Reserved Instance: Provides regional billing benefits rather than an Availability Zone capacity reservation. Spot Instance request: Depends on spare capacity and can be interrupted. On-Demand Capacity Reservation: Reserves matching EC2 capacity in a specified Availability Zone.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to estimate the cost of a new AWS workload before deploying it. Which tool should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Reports: Provide detailed incurred cost and usage data. AWS Health Dashboard: Reports AWS service health events rather than cost estimates. AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates prospective service charges from specified configuration and usage. AWS Cost Explorer: Primarily analyzes actual cost and usage data and forecasts based on it.

quiz_elements.question: A finance analyst wants graphs showing monthly AWS spending by service and a forecast based on historical usage. Which tool should the analyst use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS License Manager: Tracks licensing rather than providing billing trend charts. AWS Cost Explorer: Provides cost visualizations, filtering, and forecasts based on usage data. AWS Pricing Calculator: Models proposed service configurations rather than analyzing historical spending. AWS Health Dashboard: Shows service health rather than historical spending.

quiz_elements.question: A project manager wants an email notification when actual or forecasted monthly AWS spending exceeds a defined threshold. Which service should the manager use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Budgets: Tracks spending against configured limits and sends threshold notifications. AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates proposed costs and does not serve as the threshold alert service. AWS Cost Explorer: Cost Explorer analyzes and forecasts spending, but AWS Budgets is the service for configured budget threshold notifications. AWS Cost and Usage Reports: Reports export detailed billing data and are not the configured threshold alert service.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to detect unusual AWS spending patterns without defining a fixed threshold for every service. Which AWS capability should it use?
answers: AWS Budgets with a fixed monthly limit
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates proposed usage rather than detecting anomalous incurred spending. AWS Budgets with a fixed monthly limit: A fixed budget compares costs against a selected amount rather than learning unusual patterns. AWS Cost and Usage Reports: Reports export billing data; they do not by themselves detect anomalies. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection: Uses learned spending patterns to detect unusual costs.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs detailed AWS billing line items in Amazon S3 for analysis with its own reporting tools. Which resource meets this need?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Reports: Provide detailed billing line items and usage data delivered to an S3 bucket for custom analysis. AWS Cost Explorer: Offers interactive spending analysis and forecasts; it is not the detailed billing line-item export to S3 described. AWS Budgets: Tracks actual or forecasted spending against limits and sends alerts rather than delivering detailed billing line items. AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates prospective service costs rather than exporting incurred billing line items.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to group AWS charges by project. It adds a Project tag to supported resources. What additional billing step is required to use this tag for cost allocation?
answers: Activate the Project tag as a cost allocation tag
Apply the Project resource tag without activating it for billing
Add the Project tag to a tag-based IAM access policy
Create an AWS Cost Category without activating the Project tag
quiz_elements.explanation: Activate the Project tag as a cost allocation tag: Activation enables billing reports to use the supported resource tag for cost attribution. Apply the Project resource tag without activating it for billing: Resource tagging alone does not activate the tag as a billing cost allocation dimension. Add the Project tag to a tag-based IAM access policy: An IAM policy can use tags for authorization; it does not activate cost allocation tags. Create an AWS Cost Category without activating the Project tag: Cost Categories organize billing costs but do not replace activating a resource tag for cost allocation.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Activate the Project tag as a cost allocation tag

quiz_elements.question: Which AWS Support option is included for all AWS customers?
quiz_elements.explanation: Basic Support: Is included and provides customer service and self-service resources. AWS Business Support+: Is an additional support plan rather than the universally included option. AWS Enterprise Support: Provides additional designated expertise rather than being included for every customer. AWS Unified Operations: Provides enhanced operational services rather than being universally included.

quiz_elements.question: A company runs production workloads and wants the minimum support plan that AWS currently recommends for production. Which plan should it choose?
quiz_elements.explanation: Basic Support: Does not provide the production technical support offering described. AWS Enterprise Support: Offers more extensive guidance and is not the minimum recommended production plan. AWS Unified Operations: Offers enhanced mission-critical operational support and is not the minimum production plan. AWS Business Support+: Is the current minimum recommended AWS support plan for production workloads.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs a designated Technical Account Manager for proactive guidance on business-critical AWS workloads. Which support plan meets this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Business Support+: Provides technical support but does not include a designated TAM. AWS re:Post community access: Provides community knowledge rather than a designated account manager. AWS Enterprise Support: Provides a designated Technical Account Manager and proactive guidance. Basic Support: Provides customer service and self-service resources without a designated TAM.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs continuous workload monitoring with designated specialist expertise for mission-critical workloads. Which current AWS Support offering is designed for this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support: Provides proactive account guidance but not the continuous workload monitoring listed for Unified Operations. AWS Unified Operations: Provides enhanced mission-critical operational support, designated specialists, and continuous workload monitoring. Basic Support: Provides baseline customer service and self-service resources. AWS Business Support+: Provides production technical support rather than continuous workload monitoring.

quiz_elements.question: An operations team wants to see AWS service events that affect its account resources and receive relevant alerts. Which service should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Health: Provides personalized service health events and affected-resource information. AWS Cost Explorer: Analyzes costs rather than service health events. AWS Marketplace: Provides third-party products rather than account health events. AWS License Manager: Manages software licensing rather than service health.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants AWS best-practice recommendations that can help identify opportunities to reduce costs and improve its environment. Which service should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator: Estimates proposed costs rather than evaluating the running environment. AWS Support Center: Manages support cases rather than itself running environment checks. AWS Organizations: Manages accounts and governance rather than providing these best-practice checks. AWS Trusted Advisor: Evaluates the environment and provides best-practice recommendations across optimization areas.

quiz_elements.question: A developer wants to ask a technical AWS question and read answers from the AWS community. Which resource should the developer use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer: Analyzes cost and usage rather than community questions. AWS Organizations: Manages accounts rather than technical community discussions. AWS re:Post: Provides AWS community questions, answers, and knowledge resources. AWS Artifact: Provides compliance reports and agreements rather than community discussions.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to find and purchase a third-party security product that can run on AWS. Which AWS resource should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Cloud Adoption Framework: Provides transformation guidance rather than a software marketplace. AWS Marketplace: Offers third-party software and related purchasing and deployment options. AWS Artifact: Provides AWS compliance documents rather than a software catalog. AWS Health Dashboard: Reports health events rather than offering third-party products.

quiz_elements.question: A company receives malicious traffic that appears to originate from AWS resources. Which AWS team should it contact to report suspected abuse?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Trust and Safety: Handles reports of suspected abuse of AWS resources. AWS Billing: Handles account billing matters rather than abuse reports. AWS Professional Services: Provides consulting engagements rather than abuse handling. AWS Partner Network: Supports AWS partners rather than acting as the abuse reporting team.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants the AWS collection organized around prescriptive migration strategies, implementation guides, and reusable patterns. Which resource should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Publishes prescriptive strategies, implementation guides, and reusable patterns for migration and modernization. AWS Architecture Center: Provides reference architectures and architecture resources; Prescriptive Guidance is the specifically named collection of prescriptive strategies, guides, and patterns. AWS re:Post community questions: Offers community answers and knowledge articles rather than the prescriptive strategy, guide, and pattern collection described. Individual AWS service documentation: Provides service-specific references and instructions rather than the cross-project prescriptive migration collection described.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to work with an external consulting organization that has AWS expertise to integrate its systems and deliver a migration project. Which resource should it use to identify suitable partners?
answers: AWS Marketplace seller product reviews alone
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Partner Network: Helps customers identify AWS partners with integration and consulting expertise. AWS Marketplace seller product reviews alone: Reviews can help assess products, but the Partner Network directly identifies partners by expertise for an integration engagement. AWS Support case severity levels: Severity guides support response rather than locating an external systems integrator. AWS Architecture Center reference diagrams: Diagrams provide technical guidance rather than a partner discovery network.

quiz_elements.question: A new customer wants to understand whether an AWS Free Tier offer will cover its planned usage. What should the customer check?
answers: The account support plan as the deciding factor for all free usage
The projected compute usage while excluding request, storage, and transfer usage
The current account plan, credit conditions, and service usage limits
The legacy twelve-month offer categories without checking when the account was created
quiz_elements.explanation: The current account plan, credit conditions, and service usage limits: Coverage depends on the applicable program, account eligibility, credits, and service offer conditions. The legacy twelve-month offer categories without checking when the account was created: New and existing account programs can differ; old offer summaries alone are insufficient. The account support plan as the deciding factor for all free usage: Support entitlement does not establish the Free Tier coverage of planned service usage. The projected compute usage while excluding request, storage, and transfer usage: A complete coverage check must consider all applicable usage dimensions.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: The current account plan, credit conditions, and service usage limits

quiz_elements.question: Which statements describe consolidated billing in AWS Organizations? (Select TWO.)
answers: Consolidated billing gives every member account access to every other account resource
Each member account must use the same application architecture
Consolidated billing requires a separate additional subscription fee
The management account pays the charges of member accounts
Combined eligible usage can provide shared volume and commitment discounts
quiz_elements.explanation: Consolidated billing requires a separate additional subscription fee: AWS offers consolidated billing without an extra fee. The management account pays the charges of member accounts: The organization management account handles payment for the organization. Combined eligible usage can provide shared volume and commitment discounts: Aggregation can share qualifying discounts across accounts. Consolidated billing gives every member account access to every other account resource: Billing consolidation does not grant cross-account resource access. Each member account must use the same application architecture: Billing consolidation does not require identical workloads.
correct_answers: The management account pays the charges of member accounts
Combined eligible usage can provide shared volume and commitment discounts

quiz_elements.question: Which statements about AWS data transfer pricing are generally correct? (Select TWO.)
answers: Data transfer between AWS Regions can incur charges
All data transfer within one Region is always free
All transfer out to the internet is unlimited and free
A Savings Plan eliminates all networking charges
Data transfer into AWS from the internet is generally free
quiz_elements.explanation: Data transfer into AWS from the internet is generally free: Inbound internet transfer is generally not charged, subject to service-specific terms. Data transfer between AWS Regions can incur charges: Cross-Region transfer can be billable and requires checking the applicable service rates. All data transfer within one Region is always free: Some same-Region paths, including certain cross-AZ paths, incur charges. All transfer out to the internet is unlimited and free: Outbound internet transfer can incur charges after applicable allowances. A Savings Plan eliminates all networking charges: Savings Plans do not waive all data transfer fees.
correct_answers: Data transfer into AWS from the internet is generally free
Data transfer between AWS Regions can incur charges

quiz_elements.question: A company compares storage tiers for archive data. Which factors should it consider when estimating the total cost? (Select TWO.)
answers: The storage price and any minimum storage duration
Retrieval charges and the required access frequency
Only the number of AWS accounts in the organization
Only the company chosen support case severity
The assumption that every tier has identical retrieval pricing
quiz_elements.explanation: Retrieval charges and the required access frequency: Access patterns and retrieval charges can change the cheapest suitable option. Only the number of AWS accounts in the organization: Account count alone does not determine storage and retrieval charges. Only the company chosen support case severity: Support severity does not define storage tier charges. The assumption that every tier has identical retrieval pricing: Retrieval pricing differs between storage classes. The storage price and any minimum storage duration: Per-unit rates and minimum duration charges can affect the total.
correct_answers: The storage price and any minimum storage duration
Retrieval charges and the required access frequency

quiz_elements.question: Which statements correctly describe AWS cost allocation tags? (Select TWO.)
answers: Tags reserve capacity for the resources assigned to each project
Customers can define tags such as a project or cost center
AWS-generated tags can provide additional cost allocation information
Every tag automatically appears in billing allocation without activation
Tags create the service usage discounts shared across organization accounts
quiz_elements.explanation: Every tag automatically appears in billing allocation without activation: Cost allocation tags must be activated for billing use. Tags create the service usage discounts shared across organization accounts: Discounts come from eligible purchasing and usage aggregation rather than tags. Tags reserve capacity for the resources assigned to each project: Tagging does not reserve service capacity. Customers can define tags such as a project or cost center: User-defined tags support business-specific cost allocation. AWS-generated tags can provide additional cost allocation information: AWS-generated tags complement user-defined tags where supported and activated.
correct_answers: Customers can define tags such as a project or cost center
AWS-generated tags can provide additional cost allocation information

quiz_elements.question: Which resources provide self-service AWS technical information? (Select TWO.)
answers: AWS Knowledge Center on AWS re:Post
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator cost estimates: Provide cost estimates rather than general technical reference material. AWS Cost and Usage Reports: Provide cost and usage data rather than technical how-to content. AWS service documentation: Provides official instructions and technical references. AWS Knowledge Center on AWS re:Post: Provides technical answers and troubleshooting articles. AWS consolidated billing invoices: Provide charge information rather than technical guidance.
correct_answers: AWS service documentation
AWS Knowledge Center on AWS re:Post

quiz_elements.question: Which statements describe current AWS Support resources and access? (Select TWO.)
answers: Basic Support includes a designated Technical Account Manager
AWS Health events provide detailed application performance metrics
AWS Support Center is the catalog for buying third-party software
AWS Support Center provides a place to create and manage support cases
The AWS Health API provides programmatic access to AWS Health information for eligible support plans
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Support Center is the catalog for buying third-party software: AWS Marketplace is the third-party product catalog; Support Center manages support cases. AWS Support Center provides a place to create and manage support cases: Available case types depend on the account support plan. The AWS Health API provides programmatic access to AWS Health information for eligible support plans: Health API access is included with the current eligible paid support plans. Basic Support includes a designated Technical Account Manager: A designated TAM is an advanced support-plan feature. AWS Health events provide detailed application performance metrics: Health reports AWS service events; application performance metrics are typically observed with monitoring tools such as CloudWatch.
correct_answers: AWS Support Center provides a place to create and manage support cases
The AWS Health API provides programmatic access to AWS Health information for eligible support plans

quiz_elements.question: A company runs its payroll software on Amazon EC2. Who is responsible for installing security updates on the instance operating system?
quiz_elements.explanation: The customer: Customers manage the guest operating system on EC2. AWS: AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, rather than the customer-managed guest OS. The AWS Marketplace seller: Purchasing software does not transfer the EC2 guest OS responsibility to a seller. The AWS Support team: Support guidance does not replace the customer responsibility to patch the guest OS.

quiz_elements.question: A company is reviewing controls for the buildings that host AWS infrastructure. Which control does AWS manage?
answers: Restricting physical access to AWS data centers
Approving employee access to company S3 objects
quiz_elements.explanation: Restricting physical access to AWS data centers: AWS operates and protects its facilities. Approving employee access to company S3 objects: The customer defines access to its data. Selecting permissions for application roles: The customer sets workload permissions. Classifying the company's confidential records: The customer owns its data classification.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Restricting physical access to AWS data centers

quiz_elements.question: A company replaces a database on Amazon EC2 with Amazon RDS. Which security task is transferred to AWS?
answers: Choosing the database access permissions for applications
Managing the operating system that hosts the database
Deciding which employees may access the data
Classifying data stored in database tables
quiz_elements.explanation: Managing the operating system that hosts the database: RDS manages the underlying operating system. Deciding which employees may access the data: The customer remains responsible for data access. Classifying data stored in database tables: The customer remains responsible for its data classification. Choosing the database access permissions for applications: The customer still controls application access to its database.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Managing the operating system that hosts the database

quiz_elements.question: A company uses AWS Lambda to process customer records. Which responsibility remains with the company?
answers: Controlling physical access to Lambda facilities
Securing its function code and permissions to customer data
Replacing failed servers that run Lambda
quiz_elements.explanation: Securing its function code and permissions to customer data: Customers secure their application logic and configured access. Replacing failed servers that run Lambda: AWS operates the underlying infrastructure. Controlling physical access to Lambda facilities: AWS secures its data centers. Maintaining the virtualization infrastructure: AWS manages the infrastructure used by its managed services.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Securing its function code and permissions to customer data

quiz_elements.question: An organization stores confidential documents in Amazon S3. Which task is the organization responsible for?
answers: Maintaining disk hardware used by S3
Choosing who is allowed to read the documents
quiz_elements.explanation: Choosing who is allowed to read the documents: The customer configures permissions for its data. Maintaining disk hardware used by S3: AWS operates the storage infrastructure. Replacing S3 storage servers: AWS maintains the managed service infrastructure. Securing the physical S3 facilities: AWS manages physical security.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Choosing who is allowed to read the documents

quiz_elements.question: Under the shared responsibility model, who decides which inbound connections are allowed by an Amazon EC2 security group?
answers: The customer who configures the security group
AWS as the owner of the physical network
AWS as the provider of the guest operating system
quiz_elements.explanation: The customer who configures the security group: The customer sets the security group rules for its instances. AWS as the owner of the physical network: AWS protects infrastructure, while customers configure their virtual access rules. AWS as the provider of the guest operating system: Customers manage the EC2 guest OS and security group configuration. The AWS compliance auditor: An auditor assesses controls rather than choosing customer network rules.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: The customer who configures the security group

quiz_elements.question: Why does a customer have different security responsibilities when using Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS?
answers: AWS Support plan selection determines who patches the guest operating system
The services expose different amounts of infrastructure management to the customer
RDS makes the customer responsible for AWS data center security
EC2 removes the customer's responsibility for application data
quiz_elements.explanation: The services expose different amounts of infrastructure management to the customer: Managed services shift underlying infrastructure tasks to AWS. RDS makes the customer responsible for AWS data center security: Physical facilities remain an AWS responsibility. EC2 removes the customer's responsibility for application data: Customers retain responsibility for their data. AWS Support plan selection determines who patches the guest operating system: Service choice determines this responsibility, rather than the support plan.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: The services expose different amounts of infrastructure management to the customer

quiz_elements.question: A business chooses an AWS service that is included in a compliance program. What should the business understand about its own compliance obligations?
answers: AWS assumes all responsibility for the business's data handling policies
Only the AWS Support plan must be reviewed before storing regulated data
It must still configure and use the service to meet its applicable requirements
AWS certification makes every workload on that service compliant
quiz_elements.explanation: It must still configure and use the service to meet its applicable requirements: AWS compliance does not automatically make a customer workload compliant. AWS certification makes every workload on that service compliant: Customer configurations and usage still matter. AWS assumes all responsibility for the business's data handling policies: The customer retains responsibility for data use and controls. Only the AWS Support plan must be reviewed before storing regulated data: Compliance requirements involve services, configurations, and customer controls, rather than support plan selection alone.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: It must still configure and use the service to meet its applicable requirements

quiz_elements.question: AWS and a customer each train their own personnel on security practices. How is this control treated in the shared responsibility model?
answers: A control that applies only to on-premises environments
A shared control implemented separately by each party
quiz_elements.explanation: A shared control implemented separately by each party: Each party provides training for its own employees. An AWS-only control: Customers also train their personnel. A customer-only control: AWS also trains its personnel. A control that applies only to on-premises environments: Training remains relevant for cloud operations.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: A shared control implemented separately by each party

quiz_elements.question: A retailer must decide which of its records contain personal information before moving them to AWS. Who owns this decision?
answers: AWS because it operates the storage hardware
AWS Artifact because it publishes compliance reports
AWS CloudTrail because it records account activity
quiz_elements.explanation: The retailer: Customers own the classification and handling of their data. AWS because it operates the storage hardware: Infrastructure ownership does not transfer data classification responsibility. AWS Artifact because it publishes compliance reports: Artifact provides reports rather than classifying customer data. AWS CloudTrail because it records account activity: Activity logging does not decide data classification.

quiz_elements.question: An employee needs to view monthly reports in one S3 bucket. Which access approach follows the principle of least privilege?
answers: Share the root user credentials with the employee
Allow the required read operations on that bucket
Grant administrator permissions across the account
Allow every S3 operation on every bucket
quiz_elements.explanation: Allow the required read operations on that bucket: Grant only the actions and resources required for the task. Grant administrator permissions across the account: Administrator access includes many unnecessary permissions. Allow every S3 operation on every bucket: This exceeds the required actions and resources. Share the root user credentials with the employee: Root access is excessive and should be protected.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Allow the required read operations on that bucket

quiz_elements.question: An application on Amazon EC2 must read records from Amazon DynamoDB. Which approach follows AWS guidance for providing credentials?
answers: Configure a shared root user access key on the instance
Give the application an IAM user console password
Use an IAM role with the required permissions for the EC2 workload
Embed an IAM user access key in the application source code
quiz_elements.explanation: Use an IAM role with the required permissions for the EC2 workload: Roles provide temporary workload credentials. Embed an IAM user access key in the application source code: Embedded long-term credentials are a poor security practice. Configure a shared root user access key on the instance: Root credentials are excessively privileged and should not be distributed to workloads. Give the application an IAM user console password: A console password is not the appropriate credential mechanism for this workload.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Use an IAM role with the required permissions for the EC2 workload

quiz_elements.question: An external auditor needs temporary read access to resources in a company's AWS account. The auditor uses a different AWS account. Which IAM capability is appropriate?
answers: An IAM group shared between both accounts
A security group that lists the auditor's account ID
quiz_elements.explanation: A cross-account IAM role: A trusted external principal can assume a role with limited permissions. An IAM group shared between both accounts: IAM user groups do not span accounts or act as assumable identities. The company's root user password: Sharing root credentials provides unnecessary privileges and weak accountability. A security group that lists the auditor's account ID: Security groups control network traffic rather than IAM cross-account authorization.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants employees to sign in once and access the AWS accounts assigned to them. Which service provides centralized workforce access?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center: It provides centralized workforce access to multiple AWS accounts and applications. Amazon Cognito: Cognito primarily supports identities for customer-facing applications. AWS Secrets Manager: It stores and manages secrets rather than workforce account assignments. AWS Artifact: It provides compliance documentation rather than employee sign-in.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants employees to access AWS using identities from its existing corporate identity provider. Which concept supports this requirement?
answers: Using AWS Config as the identity directory
Sharing an IAM user among all employees
Using an S3 bucket policy as the identity provider
quiz_elements.explanation: Identity federation: Federation trusts an external identity provider and allows users to obtain role sessions. Sharing an IAM user among all employees: A shared user does not preserve individual corporate identities. Using an S3 bucket policy as the identity provider: A bucket policy authorizes resource access rather than authenticating corporate users. Using AWS Config as the identity directory: Config records and evaluates resource configuration.

quiz_elements.question: Which AWS access management activity is an example of authorization?
answers: Validating a response from an MFA device
Confirming identity with an external identity provider
Evaluating whether an IAM role may delete an S3 object
Checking a user's password during sign-in
quiz_elements.explanation: Evaluating whether an IAM role may delete an S3 object: Authorization determines permitted actions. Checking a user's password during sign-in: A password verifies identity through authentication. Validating a response from an MFA device: MFA verifies identity rather than defining allowed actions. Confirming identity with an external identity provider: An identity provider performs authentication.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Evaluating whether an IAM role may delete an S3 object

quiz_elements.question: An administrator creates an IAM user. The user has no attached permissions policies, no group memberships, and no resource-based policies granting access. What access does the user have by default?
answers: Read-only access to every AWS service
Full access to services in the creation Region
The same permissions as the administrator who created the user
quiz_elements.explanation: No permissions to AWS resources: New IAM users receive no permissions by default. Read-only access to every AWS service: Read-only permissions must be granted. Full access to services in the creation Region: IAM user creation does not grant regional administrator permissions. The same permissions as the administrator who created the user: Permissions are not inherited from the creator.

quiz_elements.question: Several existing IAM users need the same set of job permissions. Which IAM resource can simplify assigning those permissions?
quiz_elements.explanation: An IAM user group: Policies attached to a group apply to its member users. An AWS Organizations organizational unit: An OU groups accounts, rather than individual IAM users. An Amazon EC2 security group: A security group controls network traffic. An AWS KMS key: A KMS key supports cryptography rather than grouping IAM users.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants one reusable IAM policy that it controls and can attach to several roles. Which policy type should it create?
answers: A service control policy as the only permission grant
An inline policy embedded in one role
quiz_elements.explanation: A customer managed policy: The customer controls this reusable standalone IAM policy. An AWS managed policy: AWS creates and maintains AWS managed policies. An inline policy embedded in one role: An inline policy is tied to its identity rather than reusable as a standalone policy. A service control policy as the only permission grant: SCPs limit available permissions and do not grant role permissions.

quiz_elements.question: An IAM role has an applicable policy that allows an action and another applicable policy that explicitly denies the same action. What is the result?
answers: The action is allowed if the allow policy was created first
The action is allowed if the role uses temporary credentials
The action is allowed because an allow exists
quiz_elements.explanation: The action is denied: An applicable explicit deny overrides an allow. The action is allowed because an allow exists: An allow cannot override an applicable explicit deny. The action is allowed if the allow policy was created first: Policy creation order does not override explicit deny. The action is allowed if the role uses temporary credentials: Temporary credentials do not bypass policy evaluation.

quiz_elements.question: For a use case that requires long-term IAM user credentials, what is the purpose of an access key?
answers: Encrypting all files stored in an S3 bucket
Defining the permissions an IAM user receives
quiz_elements.explanation: Authenticating programmatic requests to AWS: An access key ID and secret access key are used to sign programmatic requests. Providing an additional MFA factor: An access key is a credential rather than an MFA device. Encrypting all files stored in an S3 bucket: Encryption keys are separate from IAM access keys. Defining the permissions an IAM user receives: Policies define permissions; access keys authenticate requests.
