quiz_elements.question: A company is establishing its AWS account access practices. How should it use the account root user?
answers: Reserve root access for tasks that require root-level permissions
Use root access for all daily administration
Share root credentials with each administrator
Create root access keys for every application
quiz_elements.explanation: Reserve root access for tasks that require root-level permissions: AWS recommends restricted use of this highly privileged identity. Use root access for all daily administration: Daily activities should use appropriate workforce access instead. Share root credentials with each administrator: Root credentials should be protected rather than shared. Create root access keys for every application: Applications should use suitable roles rather than root credentials.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Reserve root access for tasks that require root-level permissions

quiz_elements.question: A business has a standalone AWS account that is not part of AWS Organizations. Which task requires the account root user?
answers: Reading objects in an S3 bucket
quiz_elements.explanation: Closing the AWS account: A standalone account requires root credentials for account closure. Creating an Amazon EC2 instance: An authorized IAM principal can launch instances. Creating an IAM role: An authorized IAM administrator can create roles. Reading objects in an S3 bucket: An appropriately authorized principal can read objects without root credentials.

quiz_elements.question: A business uses a standalone AWS account outside AWS Organizations. Which change requires root user credentials?
answers: Changing the email address used for the root user
quiz_elements.explanation: Changing the email address used for the root user: Updating a standalone account's root email requires root credentials. Updating an S3 bucket policy: A principal with appropriate permissions can update ordinary bucket policies. Changing an EC2 instance type: An authorized IAM principal can manage instance types. Creating an IAM user group: An authorized IAM principal can create groups.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Changing the email address used for the root user

quiz_elements.question: A company configures MFA for its AWS account root user. What does this change mean for existing IAM users?
answers: All IAM users automatically receive the root user's MFA device
IAM users must share the root user password
Each IAM user still has its own MFA configuration
quiz_elements.explanation: Each IAM user still has its own MFA configuration: Root and IAM users are distinct identities with separate MFA configuration. All IAM users automatically receive the root user's MFA device: Root MFA configuration does not assign MFA devices to IAM users. IAM user permissions become read-only: MFA configuration does not change authorization policies. IAM users must share the root user password: IAM users retain distinct credentials.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Each IAM user still has its own MFA configuration

quiz_elements.question: A company has IAM users with console passwords and wants to enforce a minimum password length. Which feature addresses this requirement?
answers: An AWS Organizations service control policy
quiz_elements.explanation: An IAM account password policy: The password policy can enforce password complexity requirements for IAM users. An AWS Organizations service control policy: An SCP restricts permissions rather than setting password length. An Amazon EC2 security group: It filters network traffic rather than credentials. An AWS Config configuration recorder: It records resource configurations rather than enforcing IAM password complexity.

quiz_elements.question: A security reviewer needs an account-wide list of IAM users and the status of their passwords, access keys, and MFA devices. Which feature should the reviewer use?
answers: An AWS Cost and Usage Report
quiz_elements.explanation: An IAM credential report: The report summarizes IAM user credential status. An AWS Cost and Usage Report: This report describes usage and charges. An AWS Artifact compliance report: Artifact reports describe AWS or third-party compliance rather than account IAM credentials. An Amazon CloudWatch metrics dashboard: A metrics dashboard is not the IAM credential inventory.

quiz_elements.question: Which statement correctly describes an IAM permissions boundary?
answers: It defines the IP addresses allowed through a security group
It gives an IAM user the same permissions as the root user
It limits the permissions that identity-based policies can grant to an IAM user or role
It grants all permissions listed in the boundary without another policy
quiz_elements.explanation: It limits the permissions that identity-based policies can grant to an IAM user or role: A boundary sets a ceiling for those identity-based permissions. It grants all permissions listed in the boundary without another policy: A boundary does not grant permissions by itself. It defines the IP addresses allowed through a security group: A boundary is an IAM permission control rather than a network firewall rule. It gives an IAM user the same permissions as the root user: A boundary restricts permissions and does not create root access.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: It limits the permissions that identity-based policies can grant to an IAM user or role

quiz_elements.question: An organization wants to restrict the AWS service actions available to IAM principals across several member accounts. Which control can set these organizational permission limits?
answers: An IAM user group in the management account
A password policy in each member account
A service control policy in AWS Organizations
quiz_elements.explanation: A service control policy in AWS Organizations: SCPs define permission guardrails for affected member accounts. An IAM user group in the management account: IAM groups organize users within one account rather than applying member-account guardrails. A password policy in each member account: Password policies govern credentials rather than service permissions. An AWS CloudTrail trail: A trail records activity rather than restricting allowed actions.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: A service control policy in AWS Organizations

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to protect the contents of files stored on disks from unauthorized reading. Which concept addresses this goal?
quiz_elements.explanation: Encryption at rest: It protects stored data through cryptography. Encryption in transit: It protects data while moving between endpoints. Identity federation: It supports access using an external identity provider. Resource tagging: Tags label resources rather than encrypting their contents.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to protect application data while it travels between a client and an AWS endpoint. Which approach is appropriate?
answers: Add a classification tag to the resource
Encrypt only the endpoint's storage volume
Enable MFA for an unrelated administrator
quiz_elements.explanation: Use a TLS-protected connection: TLS protects data in transit. Encrypt only the endpoint's storage volume: Storage encryption protects data at rest rather than the network connection. Enable MFA for an unrelated administrator: MFA protects identity authentication rather than the data stream. Add a classification tag to the resource: A label does not encrypt transmitted data.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs a managed service to create and control cryptographic keys used to encrypt data in AWS services. Which service meets this need?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS): KMS creates and manages cryptographic keys with AWS service integrations. AWS Secrets Manager: It manages secrets such as database passwords rather than general-purpose encryption keys. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): It manages TLS certificates rather than the cryptographic keys used for service data encryption. AWS IAM Identity Center: It controls workforce access rather than encryption key management.

quiz_elements.question: An application must retrieve a database password securely. The company also wants supported automatic password rotation. Which service is appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager: It securely stores secrets and supports supported automatic password rotation. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: It stores configuration and encrypted parameters; it does not provide Secrets Manager's native automatic secret rotation. AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS): KMS manages encryption keys rather than the application's database password lifecycle. AWS IAM Identity Center: It manages workforce sign-in rather than database password storage and rotation.

quiz_elements.question: A team wants a central store for application configuration values and encrypted SecureString parameters. Which AWS Systems Manager capability should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: Session Manager: provides secure interactive sessions with managed nodes rather than configuration value storage. Parameter Store: centrally stores configuration values and supports encrypted SecureString parameters. Patch Manager: automates patching managed nodes rather than storing application parameters. OpsCenter: tracks and helps resolve operational issues rather than serving as a configuration parameter store.

quiz_elements.question: A procurement team needs to obtain AWS compliance reports for its supplier review. Which service provides on-demand access to these documents?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Artifact: Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports and agreements. AWS Audit Manager: It collects evidence about customer AWS usage rather than serving as the portal for AWS infrastructure compliance reports. AWS Config: It records and evaluates customer resource configurations rather than distributing AWS audit reports. AWS Security Hub CSPM: It consolidates security findings and checks posture rather than providing AWS audit report downloads.

quiz_elements.question: An organization wants to reduce the manual effort required to collect evidence about its use of AWS for an audit. Which service supports this task?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Audit Manager: It automates collecting and organizing evidence for customer audits. AWS Artifact: It supplies compliance documentation about AWS infrastructure rather than collecting evidence about customer usage. AWS Config: It provides resource configuration records and evaluations, but not Audit Manager's audit evidence organization workflow. AWS Security Hub CSPM: It provides security findings and posture checks rather than the requested audit evidence management workflow.

quiz_elements.question: A team must check whether a particular AWS service is included in an industry compliance program. Where should it look?
answers: The list of AWS Regions alone
An Amazon EC2 instance pricing table
AWS Services in Scope by Compliance Program
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Services in Scope by Compliance Program: This AWS resource lists service coverage for specific compliance programs. The list of AWS Regions alone: Region availability alone does not establish compliance program scope. An Amazon EC2 instance pricing table: Pricing tables do not establish service compliance coverage. The IAM user credential report: That report covers credentials rather than compliance program scope.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: AWS Services in Scope by Compliance Program

quiz_elements.question: A company needs to provision and manage TLS certificates for supported AWS services. Which service should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): ACM provisions and manages TLS certificates for supported AWS services. AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS): KMS manages encryption keys rather than ACM's TLS certificate lifecycle. AWS Secrets Manager: It stores application secrets rather than providing the managed TLS certificate integration required here. AWS IAM Identity Center: It manages workforce account access rather than TLS certificates.

quiz_elements.question: A compliance reviewer needs an audit record of changes made through the AWS Management Console, CLI, and APIs. Which service records this account activity?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS CloudTrail: CloudTrail records activity by users, roles, and AWS services as events. Amazon CloudWatch: CloudWatch focuses on monitoring metrics and logs rather than being the account API audit service. AWS Config: Config records resource state and evaluates configuration rather than replacing the activity audit record. AWS Artifact: Artifact provides compliance documentation rather than account activity events.

quiz_elements.question: A company creates a CloudTrail trail to retain its account activity events. Which storage destination can receive log files directly from the trail?
quiz_elements.explanation: An Amazon DynamoDB table: a trail does not directly deliver its log files to a DynamoDB table. An Amazon EBS volume: a trail does not directly write log files to an attached block volume. An Amazon S3 bucket: trails support direct delivery of event log files to S3 for storage. An Amazon EFS file system: a trail does not directly deliver its log files to an EFS file system.

quiz_elements.question: An auditor wants to review how a security group's rules changed over several months. Which service provides historical resource configuration information?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Config: It records historical configurations and relationships for supported resources. AWS CloudTrail: It records account actions; Config provides the historical resource configuration view requested here. Amazon CloudWatch Logs: It stores collected logs rather than maintaining Config's resource configuration history. AWS Audit Manager: It organizes audit evidence rather than being the underlying resource configuration recorder.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to evaluate whether supported AWS resources comply with its required configuration settings. Which capability meets this need?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Config rules: Rules evaluate resource configuration against specified conditions. AWS CloudTrail trails: Trails record actions rather than evaluate resources against configuration requirements. Amazon GuardDuty findings: These report detected threats rather than custom configuration rule compliance. AWS Artifact agreements: Agreements do not evaluate customer resource configuration.

quiz_elements.question: A team wants dashboards and alarms for resource metrics, such as Amazon EC2 CPU utilization. Which service provides these capabilities?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch: It monitors metrics and supports dashboards and alarms. AWS CloudTrail: It records account activity events rather than providing the resource metrics alarm capability. AWS Config: It records and evaluates resource configuration rather than monitoring CPU metrics. AWS Security Hub CSPM: It consolidates security findings and posture checks rather than providing CPU metric alarms.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to collect and analyze log messages emitted by its application. Which service capability is appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs: It centralizes log collection and analysis. AWS CloudTrail event history: It records account management events rather than arbitrary application-emitted log messages. AWS Config configuration history: It contains resource configuration state rather than application log messages. Amazon GuardDuty findings: These are threat detection results rather than a general-purpose application log collection capability.

quiz_elements.question: A security team wants a managed service to detect suspicious activity that might indicate compromised AWS credentials or workloads. Which service should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty: It detects threats and suspicious activity using AWS data sources and protection capabilities. Amazon Inspector: It assesses workload vulnerabilities rather than being the primary suspicious-activity detection service. Amazon Macie: It discovers sensitive data in S3 rather than primarily detecting compromised credentials or workloads. AWS Config: It records and evaluates configuration rather than providing GuardDuty's threat analysis.

quiz_elements.question: A company needs automated assessments for software vulnerabilities in supported Amazon EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions. Which service meets this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Inspector: Inspector scans supported workloads for vulnerabilities. Amazon GuardDuty: GuardDuty detects threats and suspicious activity rather than being the software vulnerability assessment service. Amazon Macie: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3. AWS Shield: Shield protects against DDoS attacks rather than assessing software vulnerabilities.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to discover sensitive information, such as personal data, in its Amazon S3 objects. Which service is appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Macie: It discovers sensitive data in S3 using machine learning and pattern matching. Amazon Inspector: It assesses workload software vulnerabilities rather than classifying S3 object contents. Amazon GuardDuty: It detects threats rather than discovering and classifying sensitive S3 data. IAM Access Analyzer: It evaluates access relationships rather than inspecting stored objects for personal data.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to filter web requests that match common SQL injection patterns before they reach a supported web application resource. Which service should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS WAF: It filters HTTP requests using web access control rules, including SQL injection match capabilities. AWS Shield Standard: It provides baseline network and transport layer DDoS protection rather than SQL injection request filtering. Amazon GuardDuty: It detects threats rather than applying inline HTTP request filters. An Amazon EC2 security group: It filters network traffic by properties such as ports and addresses rather than SQL content in HTTP requests.

quiz_elements.question: Which AWS offering provides baseline protection against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks at no additional charge?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Shield Standard: It automatically provides baseline network and transport layer DDoS protection at no additional charge. AWS Shield Advanced: It is a paid offering with additional DDoS capabilities. AWS WAF: It provides configurable HTTP request filtering and incurs charges rather than the automatic baseline protection described. Amazon GuardDuty: It detects threats rather than providing this baseline DDoS mitigation offering.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants enhanced DDoS protection and access to the AWS Shield Response Team for eligible protected resources. Which offering should it evaluate?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced: It provides enhanced DDoS protection and response support subject to eligibility and support requirements. AWS Shield Standard: It does not provide the same enhanced protection and response team support. AWS WAF: It filters web requests but is not the enhanced DDoS service with Shield Response Team support. Amazon GuardDuty: It detects threats rather than providing enhanced DDoS mitigation and response team access.

quiz_elements.question: A security team wants a central view of findings from AWS security services and automated checks against security standards. Which service capability is appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Security Hub CSPM: It consolidates findings and evaluates security posture against standards. Amazon GuardDuty: It detects threats rather than being the central service for findings from multiple security providers and standards checks. Amazon Inspector: It assesses supported workloads for vulnerabilities rather than consolidating the full range of security findings. Amazon Macie: It focuses on sensitive data discovery rather than providing the requested central security posture view.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to centrally manage security policies, including AWS WAF policies, across accounts in AWS Organizations. Which service supports this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Firewall Manager: It centrally manages supported security policies across organization accounts and resources. AWS WAF: It filters web requests; Firewall Manager supplies the organization-wide policy management described. AWS Security Hub CSPM: It provides security posture checks and finding aggregation rather than administering WAF policies. AWS Organizations service control policies: SCPs restrict available API permissions rather than deploying and managing firewall protections.

quiz_elements.question: A security team wants to identify supported resources whose policies allow public or external cross-account access. Which IAM capability should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer: Its external access findings identify access beyond a configured zone of trust. AWS IAM Identity Center: It assigns workforce access rather than analyzing public and external access in resource policies. IAM credential reports: They summarize credential status rather than resource policy sharing. Amazon Macie: It discovers sensitive S3 data rather than being the IAM resource policy access analysis capability.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants AWS recommendations that highlight selected security risks and other account improvement opportunities. Which service offers these checks?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor: It provides account improvement recommendations across categories including security. Amazon Inspector: It focuses on workload vulnerability assessments rather than the broad recommendation categories described. Amazon GuardDuty: It detects threats rather than providing the general account improvement checks described. AWS Artifact: It provides compliance documentation rather than improvement recommendations.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to find and purchase security software from third-party vendors for its AWS environment. Which AWS resource should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Marketplace: It provides a catalog for finding and purchasing third-party security products. AWS Artifact: It provides compliance reports and agreements rather than a security software procurement catalog. AWS Security Blog: It publishes security articles rather than serving as the product purchasing catalog. AWS Security Hub CSPM: It consolidates security findings and posture checks rather than providing software procurement.

quiz_elements.question: A team wants articles from AWS about security practices and new security capabilities. Which resource is appropriate?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Security Blog: It publishes AWS articles on security practices and new capabilities. AWS Artifact: It provides compliance reports and agreements rather than a stream of security practice articles. AWS Marketplace: It is a software procurement catalog rather than the AWS security article publication. AWS Health Dashboard: It describes service events and health rather than security practice articles.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants an AWS resource that brings together cloud security information, services, and guidance. Which resource should it visit?
quiz_elements.explanation: The AWS cloud security website: It collects cloud security information and links to AWS resources. The AWS Health Dashboard: It reports service health and events rather than providing the general security information hub described. The AWS Marketplace software catalog: It focuses on finding and purchasing products rather than central AWS security guidance. An AWS Artifact compliance report: A report documents specific compliance information rather than collecting the range of security resources requested.

quiz_elements.question: A company collects evidence with AWS Audit Manager. Which statement about the results is accurate?
answers: The evidence supports an audit, but the company must still assess its compliance
The service has certified every control once it collects evidence
The evidence replaces an assessment of the company's policies and procedures
The collected evidence always contains every item needed for any audit
quiz_elements.explanation: The evidence supports an audit, but the company must still assess its compliance: Audit Manager organizes evidence; it does not determine or certify the company's compliance. The service has certified every control once it collects evidence: Collected evidence still needs review; evidence collection is not certification. The evidence replaces an assessment of the company's policies and procedures: Policies, procedures, and controls still need evaluation. The collected evidence always contains every item needed for any audit: Audit Manager documentation warns that collected evidence may not include every required item.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: The evidence supports an audit, but the company must still assess its compliance

quiz_elements.question: A reviewer wants to distinguish resource configuration history from records of account actions. Which pairing is correct?
answers: AWS Shield for configuration history; Amazon Inspector for account actions
AWS Config for configuration history; AWS CloudTrail for account actions
AWS CloudTrail for configuration history; AWS Artifact for account actions
Amazon Macie for configuration history; AWS Config for account actions
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Config for configuration history; AWS CloudTrail for account actions: Config tracks resource state, while CloudTrail records account activity. AWS CloudTrail for configuration history; AWS Artifact for account actions: Artifact is not an account activity recorder, and Config is the service for configuration history. Amazon Macie for configuration history; AWS Config for account actions: Macie discovers sensitive S3 data, while CloudTrail records account actions. AWS Shield for configuration history; Amazon Inspector for account actions: Shield mitigates DDoS and Inspector assesses vulnerabilities; neither pairing fits.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: AWS Config for configuration history; AWS CloudTrail for account actions

quiz_elements.question: A company compares AWS WAF with Amazon GuardDuty. Which statement correctly distinguishes their primary purposes?
answers: WAF scans software packages for vulnerabilities, while GuardDuty classifies sensitive S3 data
WAF records API activity, while GuardDuty records resource configuration history
WAF filters web requests, while GuardDuty detects threats
WAF detects compromised IAM credentials, while GuardDuty filters HTTP requests
quiz_elements.explanation: WAF filters web requests, while GuardDuty detects threats: WAF applies HTTP request rules; GuardDuty identifies suspicious activity. WAF detects compromised IAM credentials, while GuardDuty filters HTTP requests: This reverses their primary purposes; GuardDuty detects threats and WAF filters web requests. WAF scans software packages for vulnerabilities, while GuardDuty classifies sensitive S3 data: Inspector assesses software vulnerabilities and Macie discovers sensitive S3 data. WAF records API activity, while GuardDuty records resource configuration history: CloudTrail records API activity and Config records configuration history.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: WAF filters web requests, while GuardDuty detects threats

quiz_elements.question: A company uses Amazon EC2 for an internal application. Which tasks are customer responsibilities? (Select TWO.)
answers: Controlling physical entry to AWS data centers
quiz_elements.explanation: Patching the guest operating system: Customers manage the EC2 guest operating system. Configuring the instance security group: Customers configure virtual network access rules. Maintaining the host virtualization layer: AWS manages the underlying virtualization infrastructure. Controlling physical entry to AWS data centers: AWS manages facility access. Replacing failed physical servers: AWS maintains the physical infrastructure.
correct_answers: Patching the guest operating system
Configuring the instance security group

quiz_elements.question: A company uses Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. Which responsibilities remain with the company? (Select TWO.)
answers: Managing access to AWS data center buildings
Classifying the data stored in these services
Configuring appropriate access to its data
Patching the operating system that hosts its RDS database
quiz_elements.explanation: Classifying the data stored in these services: Customers own data classification. Configuring appropriate access to its data: Customers retain control over data access. Maintaining the physical storage hardware: AWS manages physical infrastructure. Patching the operating system that hosts its RDS database: AWS manages the RDS underlying operating system. Managing access to AWS data center buildings: AWS controls physical facility access.
correct_answers: Classifying the data stored in these services
Configuring appropriate access to its data

quiz_elements.question: Which practices help protect an AWS account root user that has sign-in credentials? (Select TWO.)
answers: Share the root password with all developers
Use root credentials in deployment applications
Use the root user for routine resource administration
Protect the root user with MFA
Avoid creating root user access keys
quiz_elements.explanation: Protect the root user with MFA: MFA adds protection to root authentication. Avoid creating root user access keys: AWS recommends avoiding long-term root programmatic credentials. Share the root password with all developers: Shared root credentials expose highly privileged access. Use root credentials in deployment applications: Workloads should use appropriate roles rather than root credentials. Use the root user for routine resource administration: Routine tasks should use suitable workforce access.
correct_answers: Protect the root user with MFA
Avoid creating root user access keys

quiz_elements.question: Which actions support maintaining least-privilege access over time? (Select TWO.)
answers: Remove permissions that are no longer required
Scope policies to the actions and resources needed for each task
Grant AdministratorAccess to every new employee
Retain unused access keys for convenience
Use one shared privileged identity for all workloads
quiz_elements.explanation: Remove permissions that are no longer required: Removing unused permissions reduces unnecessary access. Scope policies to the actions and resources needed for each task: Narrowly scoped permissions implement least privilege. Grant AdministratorAccess to every new employee: Broad administration rights exceed most task requirements. Retain unused access keys for convenience: Unused credentials increase exposure and should be reviewed and removed. Use one shared privileged identity for all workloads: Shared broad credentials undermine least privilege and accountability.
correct_answers: Remove permissions that are no longer required
Scope policies to the actions and resources needed for each task

quiz_elements.question: Which statements describe IAM roles? (Select TWO.)
answers: Only the account root user can assume a role
A role automatically receives administrator permissions
An assumed role provides temporary security credentials
Roles can be used to delegate access across AWS accounts
Every role has a permanent console password
quiz_elements.explanation: An assumed role provides temporary security credentials: Credentials are issued for a role session. Roles can be used to delegate access across AWS accounts: Cross-account delegation is a common role use case. Every role has a permanent console password: Roles do not have standard long-term passwords. Only the account root user can assume a role: Trusted and authorized principals can assume roles. A role automatically receives administrator permissions: A role receives the permissions defined for it, rather than automatic administrator access.
correct_answers: An assumed role provides temporary security credentials
Roles can be used to delegate access across AWS accounts

quiz_elements.question: Which statements about IAM user groups are correct? (Select TWO.)
answers: Policies attached to a group apply to its member users
A group can be nested inside another group
An EC2 application can assume a group to obtain temporary credentials
An IAM role must be placed in a user group before it can receive policies
A user can belong to more than one group
quiz_elements.explanation: A user can belong to more than one group: IAM users can be members of multiple groups. Policies attached to a group apply to its member users: Groups simplify assigning common permissions. A group can be nested inside another group: IAM groups cannot contain other groups. An EC2 application can assume a group to obtain temporary credentials: Roles, rather than groups, are assumable identities. An IAM role must be placed in a user group before it can receive policies: IAM groups contain users; roles receive their own policies.
correct_answers: A user can belong to more than one group
Policies attached to a group apply to its member users

quiz_elements.question: Which measures directly protect data using encryption? (Select TWO.)
answers: Using TLS for a connection to a service endpoint
Assigning a resource cost allocation tag
quiz_elements.explanation: Encrypting stored database data: This protects data at rest. Using TLS for a connection to a service endpoint: TLS protects data in transit. Assigning a resource cost allocation tag: A tag does not encrypt data. Downloading an AWS compliance report: A report provides evidence rather than encryption. Creating an IAM user group: A group organizes permissions rather than encrypting data.
correct_answers: Encrypting stored database data
Using TLS for a connection to a service endpoint

quiz_elements.question: Which statements correctly distinguish AWS Artifact and AWS Audit Manager? (Select TWO.)
answers: AWS Artifact evaluates every customer resource against security rules
AWS Audit Manager automatically certifies a customer as compliant
Both services replace the customer's responsibility for data access
AWS Artifact provides access to AWS compliance documentation
AWS Audit Manager helps collect evidence about a customer's AWS usage
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Artifact provides access to AWS compliance documentation: Artifact distributes reports and agreements. AWS Audit Manager helps collect evidence about a customer's AWS usage: Audit Manager automates evidence collection for customer audits. AWS Artifact evaluates every customer resource against security rules: AWS Config and security posture tools evaluate configurations; Artifact distributes documentation. AWS Audit Manager automatically certifies a customer as compliant: Audit Manager supports audits but does not itself determine or certify compliance. Both services replace the customer's responsibility for data access: Neither transfers responsibility for customer data permissions.
correct_answers: AWS Artifact provides access to AWS compliance documentation
AWS Audit Manager helps collect evidence about a customer's AWS usage

quiz_elements.question: A company wants its AWS application to use temporary AWS credentials and automate rotation of a supported database password. Which approaches meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
answers: Use AWS Secrets Manager for the database password
Use an IAM role for the workload's AWS service access
Use a dedicated IAM user access key and rotate it manually
Store the database password in an encrypted environment variable and update it manually
Encrypt a long-term IAM user access key with AWS KMS before distributing it
quiz_elements.explanation: Use AWS Secrets Manager for the database password: Secrets Manager supports automated rotation of supported database credentials. Use an IAM role for the workload's AWS service access: The role provides temporary AWS credentials. Use a dedicated IAM user access key and rotate it manually: The user access key is a long-term AWS credential rather than the temporary credential requested. Store the database password in an encrypted environment variable and update it manually: Encryption can protect a stored value, but manual updates do not meet the automatic rotation requirement. Encrypt a long-term IAM user access key with AWS KMS before distributing it: Encryption protects stored credentials but does not turn them into temporary role credentials.
correct_answers: Use AWS Secrets Manager for the database password
Use an IAM role for the workload's AWS service access

quiz_elements.question: Which service and purpose pairings are correct? (Select THREE.)
answers: AWS Artifact: collect evidence about the customer's AWS usage for audit preparation
AWS KMS: provision and manage TLS certificates for load balancers
Amazon GuardDuty: detect threats and suspicious activity
Amazon Inspector: assess supported workloads for software vulnerabilities
Amazon Macie: discover sensitive data in Amazon S3
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty: detect threats and suspicious activity: GuardDuty provides managed threat detection. Amazon Inspector: assess supported workloads for software vulnerabilities: Inspector performs vulnerability assessments. Amazon Macie: discover sensitive data in Amazon S3: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3. AWS Artifact: collect evidence about the customer's AWS usage for audit preparation: Audit Manager performs customer usage evidence collection; Artifact provides compliance documentation. AWS KMS: provision and manage TLS certificates for load balancers: ACM provides the TLS certificate lifecycle; KMS manages cryptographic keys.
correct_answers: Amazon GuardDuty: detect threats and suspicious activity
Amazon Inspector: assess supported workloads for software vulnerabilities
Amazon Macie: discover sensitive data in Amazon S3

quiz_elements.question: Which statements describe AWS WAF and AWS Shield? (Select TWO.)
answers: AWS WAF stores rotating application passwords
AWS Shield grants IAM permissions for cross-account access
Both services provide AWS audit compliance documents
AWS WAF can filter web requests using conditions such as request contents
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS WAF can filter web requests using conditions such as request contents: WAF evaluates HTTP requests against web access rules. AWS Shield provides DDoS protection: Shield focuses on protection against distributed denial-of-service attacks. AWS WAF stores rotating application passwords: Secrets Manager manages application secrets. AWS Shield grants IAM permissions for cross-account access: IAM roles and policies manage cross-account authorization. Both services provide AWS audit compliance documents: Artifact provides compliance documentation.
correct_answers: AWS WAF can filter web requests using conditions such as request contents
AWS Shield provides DDoS protection

quiz_elements.question: Which service and capability pairings are correct? (Select THREE.)
answers: Amazon Macie: assess EC2 software packages for vulnerabilities

Amazon SES: sends email rather than managing customer voice interactions.

quiz_elements.question: Developers want to compile source code and run automated tests without maintaining build servers. Which AWS service should they use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS CloudFormation: provisions infrastructure rather than compiling source code and running tests. AWS CodeBuild: compiles source code, runs tests, and creates build artifacts without maintaining build servers. AWS Elastic Beanstalk: deploys applications rather than supplying the requested standalone managed build service. AWS CodePipeline: coordinates release stages and can invoke CodeBuild, but is not itself the managed compilation engine.

quiz_elements.question: A team needs to orchestrate a release process with source, build, approval, and deployment stages. Which service should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS CloudFormation: manages infrastructure deployments but does not supply the full source-to-release pipeline. AWS CodePipeline: orchestrates release stages such as source, build, and deployment. AWS Elastic Beanstalk: deploys applications but does not orchestrate the requested source, build, and approval stages. AWS CodeBuild: performs a build stage but does not orchestrate the entire release pipeline.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants to provide employees with managed virtual desktops they can access remotely. Which service should it choose?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Connect: provides cloud contact-center capabilities for customer interactions. This does not provide the capability requested in the question. Amazon WorkSpaces: provides managed virtual desktops for end users. This meets the stated requirement. AWS Amplify: provides tools and hosting for frontend web and mobile applications. This does not provide the capability requested in the question. Amazon EC2: provides virtual servers with control over the guest operating system. This does not provide the capability requested in the question.

quiz_elements.question: A frontend team needs tools and managed hosting to build and deploy a web application. Which AWS service best matches this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Lightsail: simplifies virtual-server hosting but does not provide the requested frontend development toolchain. AWS CodeBuild: runs build jobs rather than providing frontend hosting and application development tools. AWS Amplify: provides tools and hosting for frontend web and mobile applications. AWS CloudFormation: provisions infrastructure rather than supplying the frontend development and hosting product.

quiz_elements.question: A manufacturer needs to securely connect many sensor devices and exchange device messages with cloud applications. Which service should it use?
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon SNS: publishes notifications rather than managing IoT device connections. AWS IoT Core: connects IoT devices to cloud applications and securely exchanges device messages. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: ingests streaming records but is not an IoT device connectivity and messaging service. Amazon EventBridge: routes application events rather than providing IoT device connectivity.

quiz_elements.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between AWS Regions and Availability Zones?
answers: A Region contains multiple Availability Zones.
Each Region is a single data center.
All Availability Zones share the same physical building.
An Availability Zone contains multiple Regions.
quiz_elements.explanation: A Region is a geographic area with multiple isolated Availability Zones. An Availability Zone does not contain Regions; the relationship is reversed. A Region is not a single data center. Availability Zones are physically separate and each can contain one or more data centers.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: A Region contains multiple Availability Zones.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants its web application to remain available if one Availability Zone becomes unavailable. Which deployment approach best meets this requirement?
answers: Deploy application instances across multiple Availability Zones.
Deploy all application instances in one Availability Zone.
Create several subnets in the same Availability Zone.
Use a larger instance in the existing Availability Zone.
quiz_elements.explanation: Deploying across Availability Zones reduces exposure to an outage of any single zone. All instances in one zone remain exposed to that zone failing. A larger instance adds capacity but does not add another failure location. Multiple subnets in the same zone still depend on the same Availability Zone.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Deploy application instances across multiple Availability Zones.

quiz_elements.question: A business needs a recovery environment that can operate when its primary AWS Region is unavailable. Which approach addresses this requirement?
answers: Increase the size of the primary EC2 instances.
Maintain a recovery environment in a second AWS Region.
Place the recovery environment in another subnet in the primary Region.
Create a second VPC in the primary Region.
quiz_elements.explanation: A second Region supports disaster recovery for a Region-level disruption. Another subnet or VPC in the primary Region still depends on that Region. Larger EC2 instances add compute capacity but do not protect against a Region-wide interruption.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: Maintain a recovery environment in a second AWS Region.

quiz_elements.question: A company keeps some applications in its own data center and runs other applications in AWS, with connectivity between them. Which deployment model is this?
quiz_elements.explanation: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises resources and cloud resources. A cloud-only deployment does not retain the described on-premises applications. An on-premises-only deployment does not use AWS cloud applications. Single Availability Zone describes placement within AWS rather than this deployment model.

quiz_elements.question: An application performs CPU-intensive calculations and needs an EC2 instance family suited to that workload. Which instance category should the company evaluate first?
quiz_elements.explanation: Compute optimized instances target CPU-intensive workloads. Memory optimized instances target workloads needing large amounts of RAM. Storage optimized instances target demanding local storage access. General purpose instances balance compute, memory, and networking rather than specifically targeting heavy CPU processing.

quiz_elements.question: A developer wants to upload web application code and have AWS provision the environment, including compute instances, load balancing, and scaling. Which service best meets this requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS CodeBuild: compiles source code, runs tests, and creates build artifacts without maintaining build servers. This does not provide the capability requested in the question. AWS Elastic Beanstalk: deploys application code and handles environment provisioning, load balancing, and scaling for supported application platforms. This meets the stated requirement. Amazon Lightsail: offers simplified virtual private servers with bundled resources and predictable plans. This does not provide the capability requested in the question. AWS CloudFormation: provisions and updates infrastructure from declarative templates. This does not provide the capability requested in the question.

quiz_elements.question: An application writes temporary scratch data to an EC2 instance store volume. What happens to that data when the instance is stopped?
answers: The volume can be attached to another EC2 instance.
The data is automatically copied to Amazon S3.
The volume becomes a persistent EBS volume.
The instance store data is lost.
quiz_elements.explanation: Instance store data does not persist when its instance is stopped. AWS does not automatically copy it to S3, so the application must preserve needed data itself. Stopping does not convert instance store into EBS. Instance store volumes cannot be detached and attached to another instance.
quiz_elements.correct_answer: The instance store data is lost.

quiz_elements.question: A company stores objects larger than 128 KB with unpredictable access patterns. It wants S3 to automatically move them between access tiers to optimize storage costs. Which storage class should it choose?
quiz_elements.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors eligible objects and automatically moves them between access tiers. S3 Standard does not automatically change access tiers. S3 One Zone-IA is a fixed infrequent-access class in one Availability Zone. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is a fixed archive class and requires restore before access.

quiz_elements.question: A company must retain records for years. The records are rarely read, and the company can wait many hours to retrieve them. Which S3 class is designed for this long-term archive requirement?
quiz_elements.explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is designed for long-term, rarely accessed data with retrieval delays. S3 Standard targets frequently accessed objects. S3 Standard-IA provides immediate access for infrequently accessed data. S3 Express One Zone targets low-latency access rather than archival retention.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants S3 to transition eligible objects to a lower-cost storage class after a defined age and delete them when their retention period ends. Which feature should it configure?
quiz_elements.explanation: S3 Lifecycle rules automate object transitions and expiration according to configured conditions. Versioning retains multiple versions rather than defining age-based transitions. Bucket policies control permissions. Access points provide named access endpoints and associated permissions, not storage-age management.

quiz_elements.question: A request passes through several microservices before reaching a database. Developers need to trace that request and identify which downstream call causes delays. Which AWS service provides this capability?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS CodeBuild: builds and tests code rather than tracing requests across microservices. AWS CodePipeline: orchestrates software releases rather than identifying request latency bottlenecks. Amazon EventBridge: routes application events rather than collecting distributed request traces. AWS X-Ray: collects distributed request traces to help locate application bottlenecks.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants an RDS database deployment that supports automatic failover if its primary Availability Zone fails. Which option should it evaluate?
answers: A larger database instance in the same Availability Zone
An RDS read replica used only for reporting
An S3 bucket for exporting reports
quiz_elements.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ deployments provide availability and failover across Availability Zones. A reporting read replica is primarily for read scaling and is not equivalent to configured Multi-AZ automatic failover. A larger instance stays exposed to the same zone failure. Exporting reports to S3 does not provide database failover.

quiz_elements.question: A company wants users to access a centrally hosted desktop application through a web browser without installing the application locally. Which service provides managed application streaming?
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Amplify: provides tools and hosting for frontend web and mobile applications. This does not provide the capability requested in the question. Amazon WorkSpaces Applications (formerly Amazon AppStream 2.0): streams desktop applications to users through supported clients or web browsers. This meets the stated requirement. Amazon Connect: provides cloud contact-center capabilities for customer interactions. This does not provide the capability requested in the question. Amazon WorkSpaces: provides managed virtual desktops for end users. This does not provide the capability requested in the question.

quiz_elements.question: Which options are purpose-built interfaces for calling AWS service APIs from shell commands or programming-language libraries? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS CLI: allows AWS services to be controlled with commands and scripts. This satisfies the requested category or capability. AWS SDKs: provide programming-language libraries for calling AWS service APIs from application code. This satisfies the requested category or capability. AWS Management Console: provides a browser-based graphical interface for managing AWS resources. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon Quick Sight (formerly Amazon QuickSight): provides business intelligence dashboards and data visualizations. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon WorkSpaces: provides managed virtual desktops for end users. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: AWS CLI
AWS SDKs

quiz_elements.question: Which services provide general container orchestration, either AWS-native or Kubernetes-based? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Batch: schedules batch jobs rather than general ECS or Kubernetes container orchestration. Amazon EKS: provides managed Kubernetes for container orchestration. AWS Lambda: runs event-driven functions rather than a general container orchestration platform. Amazon ECS: orchestrates containerized applications using AWS container management. AWS Fargate: is compute capacity used by ECS or EKS, rather than a separate orchestration service.
correct_answers: Amazon ECS
Amazon EKS

quiz_elements.question: Which options provide serverless execution for event-driven functions and serverless compute capacity for Amazon ECS tasks, respectively? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Lambda provides serverless execution for event-driven functions. AWS Fargate provides serverless compute capacity for ECS tasks. Amazon EC2 supplies virtual servers that require guest operating system and fleet administration. Amazon ECS orchestrates containers but is not the compute capacity option itself. Amazon EKS provides Kubernetes orchestration rather than the requested ECS compute capacity or event-driven function runtime.
correct_answers: AWS Lambda
AWS Fargate

quiz_elements.question: Which AWS database services provide relational database capabilities? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon RDS: manages relational database infrastructure and common database administration tasks. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon Aurora: provides a managed relational database compatible with MySQL or PostgreSQL. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon DynamoDB: provides a serverless NoSQL key-value and document database. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon ElastiCache: provides managed in-memory caching with Valkey, Redis OSS, or Memcached. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon S3: stores data as objects in buckets. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: Amazon RDS
Amazon Aurora

quiz_elements.question: Which services are appropriate for managing shared file systems rather than object buckets or block volumes? (Select TWO.)
answers: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon EFS: provides elastic shared file storage accessed using NFS. Amazon S3: provides object storage rather than a managed file system. Amazon EC2 instance store: provides temporary local block devices rather than a managed shared file system. Amazon EBS: provides block volumes rather than shared file-system access. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server: provides managed Windows file systems with SMB access and Active Directory integration.
correct_answers: Amazon EFS
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

quiz_elements.question: Which services provide connectivity between a company network and AWS? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN: connects networks using encrypted tunnels over an IP network such as the internet. This satisfies the requested category or capability. AWS Direct Connect: provides a dedicated network connection between customer premises and AWS. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon Route 53: provides DNS, domain registration, and DNS-based traffic routing. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon SNS: publishes messages to subscribers for fan-out messaging and notifications. This is outside the category or capability requested. AWS Glue: provides data integration, data cataloging, and extract-transform-load capabilities. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Direct Connect

quiz_elements.question: A company is building a website with global users. Which services provide DNS-based routing and content delivery through edge caches, respectively? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Route 53: provides DNS, domain registration, and DNS-based traffic routing. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon CloudFront: delivers cached content through a global network of edge locations. This satisfies the requested category or capability. AWS Direct Connect: provides a dedicated network connection between customer premises and AWS. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon EBS: provides persistent block storage volumes for EC2 instances. This is outside the category or capability requested. AWS CodeBuild: compiles source code, runs tests, and creates build artifacts without maintaining build servers. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: Amazon Route 53
Amazon CloudFront

quiz_elements.question: A company needs a queue to buffer work requests and a publish-subscribe service to notify several independent subscribers. Which services meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon SQS: holds messages in queues so producers and consumers can operate independently. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon SNS: publishes messages to subscribers for fan-out messaging and notifications. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon SES: sends application, transactional, and marketing email. This is outside the category or capability requested. AWS Step Functions: coordinates application steps through managed state-machine workflows. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon Route 53: provides DNS, domain registration, and DNS-based traffic routing. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: Amazon SQS
Amazon SNS

quiz_elements.question: A company must convert recorded speech to text and convert written notifications to spoken audio. Which services meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Transcribe: converts speech audio into text. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon Polly: converts written text into synthesized speech. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon Comprehend: extracts insights such as sentiment and entities from text. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon Rekognition: analyzes images and video using machine learning. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon Quick Sight (formerly Amazon QuickSight): provides business intelligence dashboards and data visualizations. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Polly

quiz_elements.question: A company needs to identify sentiment in written reviews and recognize objects in photographs. Which services provide these capabilities? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Comprehend: extracts insights such as sentiment and entities from text. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon Rekognition: analyzes images and video using machine learning. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon Polly: converts written text into synthesized speech. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon Transcribe: converts speech audio into text. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon Lex: builds conversational interfaces using voice and text. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition

quiz_elements.question: A data team wants to run SQL directly against S3 datasets and build interactive dashboards for business users. Which services meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon Athena: runs serverless SQL queries against data such as objects in Amazon S3. Amazon ElastiCache: provides in-memory caching rather than SQL analytics or dashboards. AWS Glue: prepares and catalogs datasets rather than supplying the SQL query and dashboard interfaces requested. Amazon Quick Sight (formerly Amazon QuickSight): provides business intelligence dashboards and data visualizations. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: provides a streaming ingestion layer rather than S3 SQL queries or dashboards.
correct_answers: Amazon Athena
Amazon Quick Sight (formerly Amazon QuickSight)

quiz_elements.question: Which services can help move database records and file datasets from on-premises systems into AWS, respectively? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS): migrates and replicates database data between supported source and target databases. This satisfies the requested category or capability. AWS DataSync: automates online transfers of file and object data between supported storage locations. This satisfies the requested category or capability. Amazon Route 53: provides DNS, domain registration, and DNS-based traffic routing. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon SNS: publishes messages to subscribers for fan-out messaging and notifications. This is outside the category or capability requested. Amazon CloudFront: delivers cached content through a global network of edge locations. This is outside the category or capability requested.
correct_answers: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS)
AWS DataSync

quiz_elements.question: Which services help automate building application code and orchestrating its release pipeline, respectively? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: AWS X-Ray: traces running requests rather than building or releasing application code. AWS CodePipeline: orchestrates release stages such as source, build, and deployment. AWS Elastic Beanstalk: deploys application environments rather than providing these dedicated build and pipeline services. AWS CloudFormation: provisions infrastructure rather than compiling source or coordinating release stages. AWS CodeBuild: compiles source code, runs tests, and creates build artifacts without maintaining build servers.
correct_answers: AWS CodeBuild
AWS CodePipeline

quiz_elements.question: A web application needs to distribute requests across healthy EC2 targets and adjust the number of instances as demand changes. Which services should it use together? (Select TWO.)
quiz_elements.explanation: Amazon CloudFront: caches content at the edge rather than scaling or balancing the application instance fleet. Amazon Route 53: provides DNS routing rather than target-level load balancing or EC2 capacity scaling. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling: adjusts EC2 instance capacity according to configured policies and demand. AWS CloudFormation: provisions declared infrastructure rather than dynamically distributing requests or adjusting capacity. Elastic Load Balancing: distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets.
correct_answers: Elastic Load Balancing
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling

quiz_elements.question: Which statements about AWS Availability Zones are correct? (Select TWO.)
answers: Each Availability Zone is a different AWS Region.
Availability Zones within a Region are physically separate locations.
An Availability Zone spans every AWS Region.
An Availability Zone can contain one or more data centers.
All Availability Zones use the same power infrastructure.
quiz_elements.explanation: An Availability Zone comprises one or more data centers and is physically separate from other zones in its Region. A zone is not itself a Region and does not span all Regions. Zones are designed with independent power infrastructure to reduce shared failure risks.
correct_answers: An Availability Zone can contain one or more data centers.
Availability Zones within a Region are physically separate locations.

quiz_elements.question: Which reasons can justify deploying an application in multiple AWS Regions? (Select TWO.)
answers: Support recovery from a Region-wide disruption.
Place deployments closer to users in different parts of the world.
Reduce all cross-Region data transfer charges.
Allow instances in different Regions to share one EBS volume.
Replace the need to replicate application data between locations.
quiz_elements.explanation: Deployments in multiple Regions can support recovery from a Regional disruption and place workloads closer to geographically distributed users. Cross-Region deployments can add data transfer charges rather than reducing all such charges. EBS volumes are scoped to an Availability Zone and cannot be shared across Regions. Deployments still need an appropriate data replication strategy; multiple Regions do not automatically synchronize application data.
correct_answers: Support recovery from a Region-wide disruption.
Place deployments closer to users in different parts of the world.

quiz_elements.question: Which S3 storage classes are designed to store object data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones? (Select THREE.)
quiz_elements.explanation: S3 Standard, S3 Standard-IA, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive store objects redundantly across multiple Availability Zones. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in one Availability Zone. S3 Express One Zone also stores data in one Availability Zone and targets very low-latency access.
correct_answers: S3 Standard
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
